issues.author: mcwitt-agent
issues.body:
The current hero checkpoint (`hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k`, step 393491) multiplies each global-layer query by `(1 + 0.1 · ln(max(n / 65536, 1)))²`, where `n` is the query's 1-based position in its document. `GrugModelConfig.to_hf_config` refuses log scaling, so the checkpoint cannot be exported, uploaded or served in vLLM. SkyRL's Megatron Grug model, which hero RL uses, applies only a fixed per-layer scale. Training in the hero's own JAX trainer, including SFT for #8089, already supports it.

Both consumers ignore unknown config keys, so an export carrying the fields would load without error at the wrong scale past position 65,536. Hero exports therefore move to `grugmoe_artifact_schema_version = 3`, which always carries the three fields (null when log scaling is off). Current vLLM, the TPU lane and SkyRL reject schema 3, and each accepts it only once it applies the factor. Exports already on disk are unaffected.

- [x] Marin PR (#11128): `to_hf_config` writes `log_scaling_n_floor`, `log_scaling_alpha` and `log_scaling_power` (null when off) and schema 3, and `from_hf_config` reads them back. Then export step 393491.
- [x] vLLM fork PR (marin-community/vllm#121): accept schema 3 and multiply Q on global layers by the factor at `positions + 1`. No kernel change.
- [ ] Build and publish a GPU wheel from the fork's `main` with marin-community/vllm#121. That `main` is on vLLM 0.30 and Torch 2.14.1.
- [ ] Bump Marin's vLLM pin (`config/external/vllm/gpu.toml`) to that wheel through refresh-fork, with the Snowball parity test. Follows #10022.
- [ ] Bump SkyRL's vLLM pin (`vendor/skyrl/pyproject.toml`), which rollout workers install. SkyRL is on an older fork line with Torch 2.13, so this is a SkyRL dependency refresh to vLLM 0.30 and Torch 2.14.1, qualified on Snowball and the hero.
- [ ] vLLM parity: a tiny fp32 model with `n_floor=16` against JAX, with a negative control; then the hero on one document over 131,072 tokens, gated on the bf16 noise measured below 65,536.
- [x] SkyRL PR (#11129): read the fields, accept schema 3, and scale Q per in-document position, including packed batches under context parallelism.
- [ ] SkyRL hero parity below 65,536: the full hero in Megatron against JAX on positions where the factor is 1.
- [x] SkyRL tiny-model parity: a tiny model with `n_floor=16` matched a JAX oracle to bf16 noise unpacked, packed CP1 and packed CP2, closer to it than to variants with an off-by-one key count or a 10% parameter error (one-off GPU check, recorded in #11129; no nightly test).
- [ ] SkyRL long-context check: per-token NLL against the JAX hero on one 100K-token document, before the first RL run past 65,536.

vLLM and SkyRL must apply the same factor, or RL rollouts past 65,536 come from a different model than the one being trained.

Part of #8435. Follows #11056.

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
`step_lock` checks for a lost lease only when its context exits ([step_status.py:235](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3ceb2e58074aeccfe2ab4f6ce89dfe73ca7e97a1/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_status.py#L235)), after the step has written its status ([step_runner.py:464-467](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3ceb2e58074aeccfe2ab4f6ce89dfe73ca7e97a1/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_runner.py#L464-L467)). A worker whose lease lapsed mid-step keeps running and writes its terminal status, and a step's record, into an output path that another worker has taken over.

Reproduce:
1. Worker A takes a step's lock and runs it. Its heartbeat stops refreshing (for example, during a long network stall) and the lease expires.
2. Worker B takes the lock, runs the step, and writes `SUCCESS`.
3. A's run later fails. A writes `FAILED`, and its failure record, over B's output, then raises `LeaseLostError`.

The step now reads as failed although B's output is complete, so the next launch reruns it. While the two overlap, both also write into the same output directory.

Expected: a worker that has lost its lease writes nothing more to the step's output. Either check the lease before each status and record write, or give each execution its own directory and publish the winner with a conditional write.

Eval policy runs hit this when two launches of the same run overlap, since they share a run path (#12298).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

The lease serializes acquisition but does not fence writes: status writes replace the shared file, and a lost heartbeat raises only when `step_lock` exits. The runner passes the same output path to inline and Fray work; lazy steps and the remote wrapper can write records before the parent sees the lease loss. Refreshing before a write would narrow the window, but a takeover can still occur between the refresh and the write, and data writes can already be in flight.

**Relevant code**
- [`step_status.py#L113-L124`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_status.py#L113-L124) — unconditional status replacement
- [`step_status.py#L242-L284`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_status.py#L242-L284) — lease loss surfaced on exit
- [`step_runner.py#L452-L473`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_runner.py#L452-L473) — shared output and terminal writes
- [`step_runner.py#L490-L498`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/step_runner.py#L490-L498) — remote record write
- [`lazy.py#L336-L375`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/lazy.py#L336-L375) — lazy record write

# Proposed Fix

Give each execution a unique staging directory beside its canonical output path. Pass that directory to inline functions, Fray jobs, lazy builders, and sweep cells so an old worker can finish writing only to its own attempt. Keep the canonical path as the step identity and store its lease, terminal state, and published attempt pointer in one atomically updated state object. Publishing SUCCESS or FAILED must compare the attempt's fencing token with the current owner in the same conditional write; a stale worker raises `LeaseLostError` and cannot replace the winning pointer. Use GCS generations, S3 ETags, and local file locking; fail closed on backends without an atomic conditional update.

Resolve successful dependencies and artifact reads through the published pointer, including records and returned paths. Keep a prior successful attempt readable during a mutable rerun until its replacement commits. Read existing completed directories as legacy outputs, but put new writes in attempt directories. Update `disk_cache` and sweep's direct status/record paths under the same rule.

Test a deterministic takeover: pause A, let its lease expire, let B publish success, then resume A through failure and record writes. The canonical status, record, and resolved data must still belong to B. Repeat with a Fray worker and a lazy artifact; test that a failed or abandoned attempt never becomes visible.

Open question: do any consumers require direct file access at the canonical output path without using Marin's artifact resolver? Those callers need an explicit migration because copying attempt data into that path would restore the race.

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
676 of the 1,055 LiveCodeBench release_v6 problems have near-verbatim copies in the hero pretraining sources ([#11503](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/11503) tracks past decontamination gaps).

The copies were found by scanning all 292 normalized hero sources. A problem counts as copied when one document contains at least 30% of the case-folded word 13-grams of its statement. Before scoring, the scan drops 13-grams shared by three or more problems or found in contest problems published before May 2023. The scan ran on the sources before deduplication and sampling, so some flagged documents may not be in the training store. Paraphrased or translated copies are not detected. The largest sources of copies are stack-v3, nemotron_code_v1/content, eai-taxonomy-code-w-dclm and nemotron_cc_v2. The 9 Codeforces problems are also in the SFT data, through OpenCodeReasoning-2. No problem was found in the RL tasks.

`livecodebench-hero-clean` evaluates the 379 problems with no copy. It uses LiveCodeBench's converter, prompts, grader, dataset pin (`0fe84c39`) and protocol settings; only the problem selection differs. The set has 349 AtCoder and 30 LeetCode problems: 95 easy, 101 medium and 183 hard.

Validation on Qwen3-8B (1×H100):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Problems graded | 379 / 379 |
| Accuracy | 0.596 ± 0.025 |
| Same 379 problems in two earlier full-LiveCodeBench runs | 0.594, 0.575 |
| Per-problem agreement with each earlier run | 91.3%, 91.6% |
| Per-problem agreement between the two earlier runs | 92.3% |
| Answers cut off by the 40,960-token context | 14, scored 0 |
| Wrong answers with code | 139, all graded with the grader exiting 0 |

The full `livecodebench` corpus identity is unchanged, so existing results stay valid. The run took 73 minutes and generated 5.3M tokens. The dataset is tagged `cc` on Hugging Face, as for `livecodebench`.

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 Design decision for this port (user, 2026-11-27): the catalog must not carry its own idea of which revision of a source is current.

Today the catalog serves a snapshot that pins each source to a dataset revision. When a declaration moves to a new revision, the served copy goes stale until a "served-catalog refresh" recomputes the projections, rebuilds the snapshot and reloads the database. The strict audit then reports the gap as a `stale-pin` finding. That added 23 blocking findings to the atlas-2026.11.27 release.

On main, there is one source of truth: the database that the curation campaign writes, through the versioned `TaskStore` from #12362. It maps each source_id to its current revision and to the records keyed to that source and content. The catalog reads it directly, with no served copy of the pins. A release is a versioned snapshot of that database, not a separate projection. Under this design the `stale-pin` finding class and the separate refresh step disappear.

Related: licence provenance is now recorded once per source at ingest and carried forward to every revision (ruling `license-provenance-at-ingest-20261127`). The same rule should apply to any record whose inputs didn't change across a revision.

issues.author: hammer
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Add loop guards for agent traces at four layers: SFT data filters, wait demonstrations, an episode stop on stalls, and a loop metric in evals. Then test the RL and decoding guards Marin already has. The design follows IFM's [`repetition_check.py`](https://github.com/ifm-ai/process_entry/blob/main/repetition_check.py) and the K2-Horizon results ([arXiv 2611.21003](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.21003v1)). The full survey of Marin's current loop guards, with citations, is [here](https://gistpreview.github.io/?3d44de572b8babfc08f96ac90a05b109).

## Background

- **SFT filter (main).** The only agent-loop filter is `has_stalled_tool_call` in `lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_normalize.py`, added in #9259. It drops a record on the third identical tool call after two identical replies, within one user turn, and fired on 101 of 210,031 sampled conversations.
  - It misses Terminus-2 traces, because terminal output is stored as user turns and each one resets the counter.
  - It misses spread-out repetition.
- **Ending episodes (missing).** Nothing ends an episode when the agent repeats itself. The rolloutengine stops only at turn, token or time limits. Terminus-2's `turn_callback` can return EARLY_TERMINATION, but no callback uses it.
- **RL penalties (unused).** Vendored SkyRL has two loop penalties, both off by default. The loop-credit penalty was swept in #9599 and no strength stood out. No recipe enables the antithrash penalty for repeated actions.
- **Doom loops (in flight).** #9691 and #12240 target repeated token suffixes at the end of a response. They don't cover repeated actions, and `loop_audit.py` lives only on branch `benfeuer/mochi-doom-ftpo`.
- **Evals (no metric).** There is no standing loop metric. #7743 measured median exact-duplicate tool-call fractions of 20–37%, but only once.
- **IFM's evidence.**
  - RL cut exact repeats inside Terminal-Bench interrupt loops from 61.8% to 0.3%. Trials with a loop barely changed, from 12.9% to 11.6%.
  - SFT demonstrations of waiting after unchanged output brought interrupt loops below 1%. In IFM's midtraining data, the agent waited 0 times out of 446 such moments.

## Proposed work

1. **IFM-style rules in `chat_normalize.py`.**
   - Reject 8 consecutive identical name+args tool calls, whatever the replies.
   - Reject a call that occurs at least 10 times, accounts for at least 30% of assistant turns, and appears in a run of at least 3 identical calls.
   - For Terminus-2 records, reject at least 8 consecutive identical normalized assistant messages when one preceding observation accounts for at least 80% of the run.
   - Keep #9259's exemption for retries that get a different reply.
   - Report fire rates per source, and hand-check a sample for precision.
2. **Wait demonstrations.**
   - Audit the SFT and midtraining mixes for what the agent does after unchanged terminal output.
   - Add Terminus-2 rows that wait or poll on long-running commands, next to the recovery rows from #10888.
   - Generate them in a real-clock environment, because ShellSim sleeps take no wall time (#10159).
3. **Stall stop in the rolloutengine.**
   - Add a stop reason such as `REPEAT_STALL` that fires after 3 consecutive identical action batches with identical observations.
   - Grade the task anyway, so work done before the stall still earns credit.
   - Add it to the #12190 port list, and either confirm or remove the "thrashing detector" that the #6341 checklist marks done.
4. **Loop metrics in evals.**
   - Merge `loop_audit.py` to main.
   - Add to the #10197 eval policy: loop count and upper bound, the exact-duplicate tool-call fraction (the #7743 method), and an interrupt-loop count on Terminal-Bench.
   - Report repeats inside loops and the share of trials with a loop separately.
5. **Antithrash ablation.**
   - Enable `antithrash` on one agentic RL recipe.
   - Add an option to apply it only to otherwise-correct trajectories.
   - Track both measures from item 4.
6. **Decoding checks.**
   - Run a paired comparison of `repetition_penalty` 1.0 against 1.1 on the snowball-sft eval and the curriculum-RL policy.
   - Land #12254 with a full set of stop tokens.

## Done when

- [ ] `chat_normalize.py` has the three IFM-style rules with tests, and per-source fire rates are posted here.
- [ ] A wait-behaviour audit of the SFT and midtraining mixes is posted, and a wait-demonstration source is in the SFT mix.
- [ ] The rolloutengine records a repeat-stall stop reason, and the #6341 "thrashing detector" entry is confirmed or corrected.
- [ ] Eval reports show loop counts, the duplicate tool-call fraction, and the Terminal-Bench interrupt-loop share.
- [ ] Antithrash ablation results are posted with both loop measures.
- [ ] Results of the paired `repetition_penalty` test are posted, and #12254 has merged.

Related: #9259, #9599, #9691, #12240, #7743, #10197, #12190, #6341, #10888, #10159, #12254.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

`has_stalled_tool_call` checks three identical calls with identical replies only within one user turn; the Terminus converter stores terminal observations as user messages, so that counter resets between shell steps. The native RolloutEngine records turns and stop reasons, then grades after the harness exits; it has no repeat-stall reason. [#12167](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12167) has merged, while [#12240](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12240) measures token suffix loops separately.

**Relevant code**
- [`chat_normalize.py#L144-L174`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_normalize.py#L144-L174) — current within-turn rule
- [`download/terminus.py#L77-L123`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/terminus.py#L77-L123) — terminal output becomes user message
- [`recorder.py#L250-L318`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/recorder.py#L250-L318) — transitions and observations
- [`engine.py#L216-L255`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/engine.py#L216-L255) — harness exit and grading
- [`agents/terminus/agent.py#L986-L1012`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/bf4b85caa09586d287b503bfa3e9f9d19393424b/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/agents/terminus/agent.py#L986-L1012) — command observation loop

# Proposed Fix

1. Define one action identity (tool name plus canonical arguments), observation identity, and Terminus message normalization against saved traces. Audit the three proposed thresholds in report-only mode across each SFT source. Publish source counts, sampled true/false positives, and the decision on how changed replies interact with the eight-call rule before filtering data.
2. Add the three filters at chat normalization, with separate counters and tests for user-message observations, nonadjacent repeats, changed replies, parallel batches, and final tool calls. Rebuild affected source artifacts only after the precision audit; link the filter PR `Part of #12264`.
3. Add a `repeat_stall` stop reason to RolloutEngine when three completed action batches and their observations match. End before the next model request and use the existing grading path so completed work keeps its score. Test changing observations, timeout precedence, and a scored stall without fabricated model turns; add the behavior to [#12190](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12190) and verify the claim in [#6341](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6341).
4. Count what the agent does after unchanged terminal output in the pinned SFT and midtraining mixes. Add a real-clock Terminus wait/poll source beside [#10888](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10888)'s recovery rows, then publish source identity, row count, and a hand audit that the waits actually allow time to pass.
5. Port `loop_audit.py` from the [#12240 branch](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/benfeuer/mochi-doom-ftpo) as a reviewed, reusable metric. Pin loop and duplicate-call denominators, report both repeats inside loops and trials with a loop, and add Terminal-Bench interrupt-loop counts to the eval report and [#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197). Baseline these metrics before any training intervention.
6. With that baseline fixed, run one antithrash ablation (including the correct-trajectory-only variant) and paired `repetition_penalty` 1.0/1.1 evals on identical prompts and decoding budgets. Report task scores, loop measures, and sampling settings together. comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 I checked the IFM rule port on `benfeuer/mochi-loop-guards` (`7191758`, `ifm_filter_audit.py`) against IFM's `repetition_check.py` (`ifm-ai/process_entry` `4aabc78`). The test data was public traces that Marin's loaders read, at pinned revisions and converted the way `agenttrove.py` and `open_swe_traces.py` convert them: 10,398 AgentTrove trajectories (`b395a43`, 15 row groups), 1,998 Nemotron-Terminal-Corpus (`a1667c4`), and 2,500 each from Open-SWE-Traces `openhands/qwen36_27b` and `sweagent/qwen36_27b` (`f967cba`).

On AgentTrove the port agrees with IFM and finds more:

- `terminus8` flags the same 34 trajectories as IFM's `max_content_dup_run`.
- `run8` and `frequent` add 4 that IFM's tool-call rules cannot see, because Terminus commands live in the message content.
- I read those 4 and 6 of the 34, and all ten are loops.

Neither the port nor IFM fired on Nemotron-Terminal-Corpus or Open-SWE OpenHands. On Open-SWE SWE-agent, `terminus8` fired once, a false positive (last point below).

**The miss: a turn with an empty command list counts as a wait.** `CommandBatch.wait_only` is `all(k == "" for k in self.keystrokes)` (`repetition.py:39-41`), which is true for `"commands": []`. This is intended: `test_repetition_identity.py:87` asserts it, and the Terminus prompt says "Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action". But the rolloutengine Terminus agent sends nothing for such a turn and waits 0 s (`agents/terminus/agent.py:923-946`). In AgentTrove these turns mostly come from a stuck agent:

- 122 of the 10,398 trajectories have 8 or more consecutive empty-list turns. The port flags 30 of them, all through `terminus8`, because `run8` and `frequent` skip waits (`ifm_filter_audit.py:68,75`).
- I read a seeded sample of 30 of the 122, and 20 are loops:
  - 9 completion ping-pongs. The model sends no command with `task_complete: true`, the harness asks it to confirm, and the model answers with no command and `task_complete: false`. This repeats until the turn cap.
  - 11 wedged runs that re-describe the same empty prompt in new words each turn.
- The port flags 6 of the 20. On the rest, the changing analysis text keeps `terminus8` silent. None of the 30 is waiting on a running command.
- The other 10 are not loops. They are MiniMax M2.0 StackExchange rows whose stored turn has `"commands": []` while the commands the harness ran are inside the analysis string.
- Counting an empty list as an action in `run8` fires on all 122, plus one loop the port misses that mixes empty lists with empty-keystroke waits.

The same test decides three other things:

- `wait_after_unchanged_output`, the audit for item 2, counts 1,798 waits after unchanged output on this sample. 1,690 of them are empty-list turns, and only 108 send an empty-keystroke wait.
- `detect_stall` never matches a window that contains a wait, so the `REPEAT_STALL` stop cannot end a wedged agent (snippet below).
- `antithrash_repeats` drops wait-only turns (`trajectory_reward_shaping.py:213-217`), so a no-op loop is never charged.

Requiring at least one command in `CommandBatch.wait_only` would let these rules see the runs and would take them out of the wait audit. It would also flag the MiniMax rows above.

**Two smaller points:**

- `loop_audit.py` goes the other way: its `run8` does not exempt waits (`loop_audit.py:204,218-220`), so it counts real polling.
  - 11 AgentTrove trajectories have 8 or more consecutive empty-keystroke waits. `loop_audit` flags all 11; the port flags none.
  - Of the 7 I read, 6 poll a build or script whose output advances, and one waits on a hung terminal.
- `terminus8` runs on every record and compares raw `content or ""` (`ifm_filter_audit.py:88`), so tool-call turns with empty content form a run. This is the SWE-agent false positive: eight consecutive `bash` calls with empty content, each a different `sed -i` edit answered by "Your command ran successfully and did not produce any output." IFM skips empty content (`quality_checks.py:975-978`), and item 1 limits this rule to Terminus-2 records.

Reproduce `wait_only` and `detect_stall` from the branch root:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=lib/rolloutengine/src python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
from rolloutengine.repetition import ActionPair, detect_stall, wait_only

def turn(analysis):
    payload = {"analysis": analysis, "plan": "", "commands": [], "task_complete": False}
    return {"role": "assistant", "content": json.dumps(payload)}

prompt = {"role": "user", "content": "New Terminal Output:\n\nroot@host:/app#"}
print(wait_only(turn("The /app directory is empty.")))  # True: the turn sends nothing
pairs = [ActionPair.of(turn("The /app directory is empty."), [prompt]) for _ in range(3)]
print(detect_stall(pairs, 3))  # False, even with identical turns and observations
EOF
```

<details><summary>Count the empty-list runs on the AgentTrove sample</summary>

Save as `repro_noop.py` at the branch root and run `uv run python repro_noop.py`. It prints `{"kept": 10398, "noop_run_8": 122, "noop_run_8_flagged": 30, "wait_run_8": 11}`.

```python
import json

import fsspec
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

from experiments.post_training.mochi_loop_guards.ifm_filter_audit import fire_rules
from marin.datakit.download.agenttrove import EXCLUDED_TASK_SOURCES, TERMINUS_THINK_TOKENS, is_excluded_teacher
from marin.datakit.download.opencode import INLINE_TOOL_CALL
from marin.datakit.download.terminus import TerminusParseMode, terminus_protocol_messages
from rolloutengine.repetition import parse_commands

URL = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-thoughts/AgentTrove/resolve/b395a4307a2bc9950a90dc899438f149e115fc60/data/train-{:05d}-of-00038.parquet"
GROUPS = [(10, 32), (18, 68), (30, 21), (10, 21), (6, 12), (28, 4), (33, 80), (27, 36), (29, 35),
          (34, 10), (34, 2), (21, 17), (5, 30), (31, 14), (33, 85)]
COLUMNS = ["conversations", "original_source", "original_teacher", "model", "model_provider"]


def longest_run(flags):
    best = current = 0
    for flag in flags:
        current = current + 1 if flag else 0
        best = max(best, current)
    return best


totals = {"kept": 0, "noop_run_8": 0, "noop_run_8_flagged": 0, "wait_run_8": 0}
fs = fsspec.filesystem("http")
for shard, group in GROUPS:
    with fs.open(URL.format(shard), "rb", block_size=4 << 20) as f:
        rows = pq.ParquetFile(f).read_row_group(group, columns=COLUMNS).to_pylist()
    for row in rows:
        if row["original_source"] in EXCLUDED_TASK_SOURCES or is_excluded_teacher(row):
            continue
        conversations = row["conversations"]
        if any(INLINE_TOOL_CALL.search(m.get("content") or "") for m in conversations):
            continue
        messages = terminus_protocol_messages(conversations, TERMINUS_THINK_TOKENS, mode=TerminusParseMode.STRICT)
        if messages is None:
            continue
        merged = []
        for m in messages:
            if merged and m["role"] == "user" and merged[-1]["role"] == "user":
                merged[-1]["content"] = f"{merged[-1]['content']}\n\n{m['content']}".strip()
            else:
                merged.append(dict(m))
        batches = [parse_commands(m["content"]) for m in merged if m["role"] == "assistant"]
        noop = longest_run(b is not None and not b.keystrokes for b in batches)
        wait = longest_run(b is not None and bool(b.keystrokes) and b.wait_only for b in batches)
        totals["kept"] += 1
        if noop >= 8:
            totals["noop_run_8"] += 1
            totals["noop_run_8_flagged"] += bool(fire_rules(merged))
        totals["wait_run_8"] += wait >= 8
print(json.dumps(totals))
```

</details>

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
Polaris's retained TaskSpecs request plain-text answers, but the packaged grader requires literal `</think>` followed by a boxed result. Correct plain-text answers and Mochi's `<|end_think|>` output therefore receive scored reward 0 with nonzero token-loss masks. This is a mismatch between the retained task/consumer contract and the intentionally preserved upstream format gate, not a failure of the mathematical equality check.

Two independent blinded reviews of 20 retained responses from Mochi campaign runs `.532` and `.534` agreed on 17 correct final answers and 3 missing finals. All 20 received 0. The larger retained population has 202/202 zeros; it has not been independently regraded.

Reproduce:

1. Extract the [frozen audit bundle](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-08a%2Fmarin%2Fusers%2Fbenfeuer%2Fmochi-rl-data-campaign%2Fpolaris-audit%2F2026.11.26.1%2Faudit-evidence.tar.gz). Install its pinned Sympy 1.13.3, pylatexenc 2.10 and mpmath 1.3.0.
2. From the extracted directory, run:

```python
import json, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "frozen-grader")
from grade import score
contract = json.load(open("cases/P-2-06/config.json"))
assert score("63", contract) == 0
assert score(r"\boxed{63}", contract) == 0
assert score(r"<|start_think|>work<|end_think|>\boxed{63}", contract) == 0
assert score(r"<think>work</think>\boxed{63}", contract) == 1
```

The same contrast reproduces for correct answers `12000` and `6` on two other tasks. Incorrect, empty and unfinished-reasoning controls return 0. This CPU repro calls the unchanged `score` function used by the CLI; local `/app` and `/tests` placement was not exercised.

Expected: the grader/binding accepts a mathematically correct answer in the task's advertised format across supported model reasoning protocols, while preserving wrong-answer and incomplete-output failures. It must not impose an undisclosed XML or boxing requirement.

Affected retained source: `open-athena/polaris-project-polaris-dataset-53k-b25e0cb8-retained-20261116-b-v1@9079512fe3d2d332b446b1b37deb9d2898f5461e`; upstream scorer revision `eda12fe22dd83aca59ec46a67147240dc483f62b`. Producer files are `experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/polaris/grade.py` and `tasks.py` on the ingestion branch. Fix forward on `benfeuer/long-loop-prototype` with a regression and re-seal/re-pin for future rounds. Existing campaign runs and records remain unchanged.

[Contract frozen before code inspection](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/issues/91#issuecomment-7207765866). comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 I ran the v4 grader over all 53,291 rows of POLARIS-53K. It raises on 1,433 of them, and 397 of those have a valid choice-label reference. It also cannot pay the correct answer in its natural form when the reference ends in a factorial (70 rows) or contains a negation word (12 rows).

Setup: `score` from `polaris_repair.grader_files()` at `334094a731`, called in process on `polaris-data-53K.jsonl` at `296f8e3413`, with math-verify 0.9.0, latex2sympy2-extended 1.11.0 and sympy 1.13.3. The config is `{"problem", "answer"}`, as the converter writes it. The first reply for each row is its own reference in a box. Line numbers count from 0.

**Rows that raise**

| raise | rows |
|---|---:|
| `InvalidTask`: math-verify cannot parse the reference | 926 |
| `InvalidTask`: "Polaris reference label and choice content disagree" | 421 |
| `InvalidTask`: "Polaris reference names an undeclared choice" | 62 |
| `InvalidTask`: "the reference parses to an undefined value" | 22 |
| `GradingInfraError`: "math verifier deadline exhausted" | 2 |

On 1,411 of the 1,433, the replies `0`, `x+1` and an empty reply raise as well. The retained release keeps 53,167 of the 53,291 rows, so at least 1,309 of the 1,433 are in the release that `source_pins.json` binds. I cannot read the release to count them exactly.

475 of the raising rows have a reference that starts with `\textbf{(X)}` for a choice the question declares. In 397 of them the text after the label is empty, or equals the declared choice once LaTeX spacing and the backslash left by a lost `\ ` are removed:

- Line 48 stores `\textbf{(D)}\20\sqrt{2}`, and choice D is `\ 20\sqrt{2}`. `math_reference` compares `\20\sqrt{2}` with the choice and raises for `D`, `20\sqrt{2}` and `\boxed{20\sqrt{2}}`.
- Line 2540 stores `\textbf{(E)}`, and choice E is `\ -1`. `E`, `-1` and `\boxed{-1}` raise.

As a check I made `math_reference` return the declared choice for those 397 rows. 341 then grade as expected: the label and the boxed choice score 1, and every other label scores 0. The other 56 have choices the comparator cannot handle, mostly sentences: 48 still raise, and 8 grade a reply wrongly.

21 of the 22 undefined references are times on the hour, such as `3:00` (line 2414) and `6:00 \text{ P.M.}`, which parse to `zoo`.

**Correct answers that score 0**

- 71 references end in `!`: `n!` on 22 rows, `10!`, `(2n-1)!!`. `final_candidate` removes the factorial sign with `rstrip(".!")` (`polaris_grade.py` L165). On 68 of them the reference scores 0 bare, in `\boxed{}` and as "The answer is n!.", and 1 only inside `$…$`. On 2 more it exhausts the verifier deadline; these are the two deadline rows above. With `rstrip(".")`, 70 of the 71 score 1 in all of those forms.
- 12 references match `NEGATION` (L152), so `final_candidate` returns no candidate for a reply that states them: `False` (3 rows), `\text{Not guilty}`, `Not\ Equivalent`, `will \ not`, and 6 sentences with "not". Each scores 0 in every form I tried. The 10 rows whose reference is `True` score 1 for `True`.

A labelled reference with a lost space can also pass the agreement check. Line 34241 stores `\textbf{(C)}\y^{2}+10y-7=0`, and the labels A, B and D score 1 as well as C.

issues.author: chrismc91
issues.body:
We are targeting an update to our post-training eval policy on November 30th, 2026\. The new policy will focus on improving coverage over key capabilities, especially factuality and math/science reasoning. The purpose of this issue is to invite the community to provide feedback on the listed evals and suggest changes to our implementations.

## Changes to In-Distribution Benchmarks

The tables below list the major changes to our the in-distribution benchmark composition.

* Benchmarks slated for **removal** will be taken out of the policy with high probability,
* Benchmarks flagged for **changes** need some repair to make them work on more recent versions of main,  
* Benchmarks marked as **potential additions** have draft implementations and may be included in the next round.

We will select our in-distribution benchmarks to collectively cover the capabilities necessary for Mochi to do well on our out-of-distribution benchmarks (listed below). Beginning in 2027, we hope to make this process more data-driven, but for the Nov 30 policy, we will select ID benchmarks based on:

1. Our assessment of each benchmark’s quality and appropriateness for hillclimbing,  
2. Whether an eval can be run reliably in our eval infrastructure,  
3. The resource cost of running the eval,  
4. The wall clock time of running the eval,  
5. Coverage over our out-of-distribution benchmarks,  
6. Whether we find eval contamination in our training data.

In the policy announcement on Nov 30, we will explain why particular evaluations were included or excluded. Our full set of in-distribution evals must run in no more than 24 hours for Mochi, and our eval lite subset used for model development must run in no more than 3 hours.

The proposed changes favor more recent evaluations (which have a smaller chance of contamination and reflect modern capability priorities) while increasing implicit weight on scientific tasks. This includes the addition of a number of benchmarks specifically targeting scientific knowledge and reasoning. New core capability benchmarks target factuality (SimpleQA Verified, FACTS Parametric/Grounding), instruction following (MultiChallenge) and realistic long context tasks (LongBench v2). We have not significantly changed the set of agentic evaluations in this round and will instead focus on reliable, performant implementations of our existing evals, with a few exceptions.

## Changes to Out-of-Distribution Benchmarks

Our previous eval policy listed AAII v4.3, Terminal Bench Science v0.1 and DeepSWE v1.1 as out-of-distribution benchmarks. We largely retain this set of evals, with some changes, notably the inclusion of LAB-Bench v2.

Below, we list the full set of evals we consider out of distribution. As a reminder, we do not run these evaluations until the completion of a Marin post-training round and do not look at any individual tasks. The single exception to this rule is the evals team that implements the public subsets of these evaluations for us to report. The evals team does not share any data from the implementation testing with the training team and will protect any data from testing runs from Marin’s training engineers and their agents.

### Public Out of Distribution Benchmarks

* AAII v4.3 and v5.0  
  * Terminal Bench Science v0.1  
  * Terminal Bench 4.0  
  * SciCode  
  * AA-LCR v1.1  
  * HLE Diamond  
  * AutomationBench-AA (public Zapier subset)  
  * AA-Omniscience v1.1 (public subset)  
  * GDPval-AA v2  
* LAB-Bench 2

## Changes to Comparison Models

Mochi belongs to a different weight class from Snowball and its competitor set needs to update accordingly. We are tentatively scoping a four-tier comparison set:

**Tier 0**: Existing Marin models (currently, Snowball)  
**Tier 1**: Strong models in a smaller weight class where Mochi should be competitive.  
**Tier 2**: A collection of peer models from other open providers.  
**Tier 3**: Strong models in Mochi’s weight class that roughly represent the open frontier.

🤖

# Research

This is a policy release spanning benchmark selection, evaluator readiness, comparison runs, and publication. The October policy in [#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) is the baseline. [#12147](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12147) is an open trial policy with no policy launcher yet; it omits SOTOPIA-hard, τ³-bench, BFCL, and BixBench because their current Harbor paths do not run. [MultiChallenge](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11757) has merged, while several other candidate implementations and the [contamination index](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10938) remain open.

**Relevant code**
- [Trial policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/64eda2932457194efc9ac438be27d584560ab4b4/experiments/evaluation/policies/marin_2026_11_20_trial/policy.py) — current trial selections.
- [Trial limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/64eda2932457194efc9ac438be27d584560ab4b4/experiments/evaluation/policies/marin_2026_11_20_trial/README.md) — known gaps and protocol differences.
- [Policy resolver](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/64eda2932457194efc9ac438be27d584560ab4b4/experiments/evaluation/policy/resolve.py) — candidate settings.

# Proposed Fix

1. **November 24–25: decide the candidate set.** Record include, remove, or defer for every benchmark in this issue. For each proposed inclusion, record the implementation PR, task/data and judge revisions, contamination check, scoring audit, reliability, expected capability coverage, and measured runtime. Resolve the four missing Harbor benchmarks explicitly; do not count the trial policy as the November release.
2. **November 25–27: make the selected set runnable.** Use #12147 and its launcher follow-up as the policy path, and track existing benchmark PRs such as [FACTS Parametric](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12146), [ARC-AGI-2](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/12149), [IMO-AnswerBench](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11764), and [SWE-Bench Pro](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/11774). Pin the selected implementations and all comparison-model revisions and serving settings. Put evaluator repairs in their own PRs.
3. **November 27–29: validate and run.** Preflight and smoke-test each selected benchmark, then measure the Mochi full and lite suites against the 24-hour and 3-hour limits. Audit scored-task coverage, grader disagreements, failures, and trace provenance. Run the 13 listed comparison models on the same pinned policy, reusing earlier results only when protocols and revisions match. Keep reserved out-of-distribution tasks outside policy tuning and run them only after the post-training round, as specified here.
4. **November 30: publish or record the gap.** Publish the versioned policy, comparison results, inclusion/exclusion rationale, measured suite times, and follow-up issues. If a required run or audit is incomplete, list the blocker and revised date here. Component PRs should say `Part of #12156`; close this issue only when its four Done When conditions are met.

comments.body:
🤖 Implementation notes on the listed evals and comparison models, checked against `main` at `6081e9b` and the open PRs' current heads. Items 1-4 can change a model comparison.

1. **Thinking-off does not reach 8 of the 12 external comparison models.** Protocols express thinking only as `enable_thinking`. In the linked repositories' chat templates, `enable_thinking=false` renders the same prompt as no kwargs for Muse Glimmer, K2 Horizon, Command A+, Solar Open 2, Mistral Large 4, Beam 1.0, Inkling 2 Small and GLM 5.3 Flash. A catalog entry can map thinking-off to another kwarg ([evaluation.py#L157-L160](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/marin/src/marin/rollouts/evaluation.py#L157-L160)), but only Glimmer has an entry. Glimmer, K2 Horizon, Mistral Large 4, Beam and GLM 5.3 Flash have no setting that turns reasoning off. MRCR, IFBench and CRUXEval grade `reasoning + "\n\n" + content` ([response.py#L31-L32](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/evaluation/response.py#L31-L32)), so MRCR scores 0 for any reply with reasoning (it must start with the nonce, [long_context.py#L36-L40](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/long_context.py#L36-L40)), and one reasoning line can turn an IFBench strict pass into 0 (key 296, `format:no_whitespace`). The 2,048-token caps of CRUXEval and SimpleQA Verified non-thinking and the 4,096 cap of LongBench v2 non-thinking can cut these models off mid-reasoning. Smallest fix: `thinking_off_template_kwargs: {reasoning_effort: none}` for Command A+, Solar Open 2 and Inkling; grade the final answer on thinking-off selections for the rest (#10828, third item); report which rows ran with reasoning. The new catalog entries also need reasoning parsers for these models' markers, because the scorers' inline fallback strips only `</think>` and `<|end_think|>`.

2. **Gemma 4 31B.** The link is the pretrained `google/gemma-4-31B`, which has no chat template. The instruction-tuned `google/gemma-4-31B-it` defaults to thinking off. SuperGPQA, GenomeQA, EconEvals, MultiChallenge and ARC-AGI-2 (#12149) send empty `chat_template_kwargs` (for example [supergpqa.py#L49](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/experiments/evaluation/benchmarks/supergpqa.py#L49)), so Gemma would answer them without reasoning while every other listed model reasons by default. Fix: serve the -it model and set `enable_thinking: true` on those five.

3. **WinoGrande and TruthfulQA MC2 contexts reach the model without BOS.** `encode_pair` encodes non-empty contexts with `add_special_tokens=False` and sends token ids ([likelihood.py#L68-L80](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/likelihood.py#L68-L80)). When I rescored gemma-4-26B-A4B-it's October campaign requests with `<bos>` added, WinoGrande accuracy rose 4.97 points [1.26, 8.68] and MC2 6.26 [3.24, 9.36]. Gemma 4's tokenizer adds no special tokens on encode, so `add_special_tokens=True` would not help. Prefixing `bos_token_id` when the chat template writes `bos_token` covers Gemma 4, Snowball, Glimmer, K2 Horizon, Command A+ and Mistral Large 4. This is #10828's BOS item.

4. **MMLU-Pro** sends the five worked examples in one user message, and the scorer reads the first `answer is (X)` ([choices.py#L23-L28](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/choices.py#L23-L28)), which can be the model's answer to the first example. On the two Grug checkpoints of #11981 (a merged checkpoint and a Snowball RL step) this gives 41.3% and 28.8%, against 74.5% and 75.5% with the examples as turns. Other models are not measured.

5. **GLM-5.3-Flash judges PHYSICS-Verified** ([evalchemy.yaml#L81-L92](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/experiments/evaluation/configs/evalchemy.yaml#L81-L92)) **and IMO-ProofBench (#11967)**, and it is a Tier 3 comparison model, so it would grade its own answers. The gpt-oss-120b judge used elsewhere avoids that.

6. **OlympiadBench** grades the first `\boxed` in reasoning plus answer, and an empty extraction skips the judge ([olympiad.py#L43-L65](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/olympiad.py#L43-L65), [main.py#L52-L53](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/6081e9b4feb1dce7a21eb54c719646369bb497ed/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/main.py#L52-L53)). The trial policy's smoke run recorded 62 empty extractions in 200 Qwen3.6 attempts (72cd9f8). This is #10828's third item.

7. **ChemBench (#11831):** the prompt's example allows a "comma- or space-separated list" (the next sentence asks for commas), but the answer regex accepts only commas ([chembench.py#L26-L29](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2abdd2c89614aa91b55da1363d415007e3930282/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/importers/evalchemy/scorers/chembench.py#L26-L29)). Written with spaces, the correct letters score 0 on all 394 rows that have more than one correct letter; with commas they pass all 2,542 multiple-choice rows.

8. **DS-1000:** see the note on #12147.

<details><summary>Reproduce 1 and 7</summary>

Item 1 (`huggingface_hub`, `transformers`; Qwen 3.8 is a control that honors the flag):

```python
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from transformers.utils.chat_template_utils import render_jinja_template

messages = [[{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2 + 3?"}]]
for repo in ("meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B", "IFM/K2-Horizon-375B-A23B", "CohereLabs/command-a-plus-05-2026-bf16",
             "upstage/Solar-Open2-250B", "mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B", "reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B",
             "thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Small", "zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash", "Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B"):
    template = open(hf_hub_download(repo, "chat_template.jinja")).read()
    default, off = (render_jinja_template(messages, chat_template=template, add_generation_prompt=True,
                                          bos_token="", eos_token="", **kwargs)[0][0]
                    for kwargs in ({}, {"enable_thinking": False}))
    print(repo, default == off)  # True: enable_thinking=false changes nothing
```

Item 7, from a checkout of #11831 with `PYTHONPATH=lib/taskcompendium/src:lib/verifyit/src`:

```python
from taskcompendium.importers.evalchemy.scorers.chembench import grade_chembench

config = {"kind": "multiple_choice", "letters": ["A", "B", "C", "D"], "correct": ["A", "C"]}
```

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 On keeping IFBench ("May Retain"): replies that ignore the request score about 40% on it. Through `python -m experiments.evaluation.trivial_replies` (#11222) on Marin's canonical IFBench corpus, `hello` passes 121 of 300 prompts (0.403 strict prompt accuracy) and `0` passes 103. Under the October tracker's graders, the single word `scrambled` scores 40.33% on `allenai/IFBench_test` and `Stopped` 43.33%. That is above all 23 Marin cells of the #10283 tracker (highest 37.3%), and `Stopped` is above its best baseline, `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` at 42.0%. #10423's fixes do not change these scores; the [IFBench audit's](https://github.com/XiaoyuanWang111/ifbench-audit) proposed checkers lower them to 16.33% and 19.33%.

The cause: 256 of the 300 prompts carry one constraint, nearly half of all constraints can be met by one word, and no check asks whether the reply addresses the request. So a checkpoint whose replies collapse to a few words gains on IFBench: `Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.17.49` step 12 passes 59 prompts with its full replies and 103 with only their first word. This does not show that gaps between real models are noise.

If IFBench stays, I'd suggest reporting a constant-reply floor beside it. The launcher above computes one under the run configuration of the model it is compared with.

**Looking for the metadata?**

- [The checked-in data references](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/datakit/hero_data.py) identify existing pipeline artifacts.
- **There is no public Hugging Face metadata release yet.** The [release proposal](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/hero-cluster22-reconstruction/docs/reproducibility/hero-metadata-release-proposal.md) describes the planned tables.

Marin’s data is reproducible in principle, but reproducing it still requires expensive scans and pipeline runs. We want a cheap path that reuses existing selection decisions, scores and embeddings.

David’s handoff completed text reconstruction for cluster 22. Our follow-up work checked output counts and stored Harrier coverage, and is adding foreign keys to original source rows or records, alongside document IDs, cluster and quality metadata, and stored vectors.

Validated metadata now covers **85 of 150 sources in cluster 22, totaling 11,527,805 selected occurrences**. This includes all selected Nemotron Code v2 **synthetic Code Review (4,932,132)**, **synthetic Rewriting (3,447,382)**, **synthetic Student-Teacher (1,150,817)** and **synthetic Transpilation (878,851)** documents, with keys to their original sources and physical rows, selection metadata and stored Harrier vectors. Full output audits checked every exported file and source coordinate for all four sources.

All **953,132 SFT Code selected occurrences** now include original source-row keys, selection metadata and stored Harrier vectors. The full output audit checked all **220 files** and **1,024,319 physical source locations**, preserving **71,187 additional row witnesses**.

All **98,589 SFT General selected occurrences** now include original source-row keys, selection metadata and stored Harrier vectors. The full output audit checked all **355 exported files** and **131,650 physical source locations**, preserving **33,061 additional row witnesses**.

QA’s original-row mappings are complete. Its final source index and vector join remain unfinished. The full cluster 22 metadata export remains in progress. Where identical text matches several upstream rows, we retain alternatives without claiming to know which historical occurrence supplied the document.

We plan to publish metadata, stored embeddings, manifests and reconstruction instructions on Hugging Face. Users should be able to retrieve upstream inputs and reconstruct the selected corpus without repeating deduplication, contamination checks, classifiers, embedding inference or clustering. Cluster 22 is the first validation target; the goal covers all 40 topic clusters.

We do not plan to republish upstream text or tokens. Retrieval stays upstream to preserve attribution and creators’ control over removals and opt-outs. Pinned revisions cannot guarantee access to removed data.

Done when the metadata is accessible, source/vector joins and selected counts are validated, and a worked reconstruction example reports time, bytes read and compute.

issues.author: davidlundgren
issues.body:
## TL;DR

A review of 7,503 sampled documents from the 10.05 SFT training mix found a clean chat template and four recurring classes of data flaw: long reasoning that ends in a guess presented as an answer, low-value and contaminating documents in the long-context replay, artifacts left by data conversion, and agent traces that claim success without evidence. Most are detectable by script. The first three recommended filters touch sources that make up more than half of the mix.

## Description

The 10.05 SFT run (`grug-67b-sft-20260929-special-token-lr-full-ab-4750-grouped`, exported as `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05`) trained on 216 SFT token stores (79.65% of training positions) and 391 pretraining replay caches (20.35%). About 80% of the mix is text generated by other open-weight models.

Method:

- **Sample:** 7,503 whole documents drawn at random from the token caches, with per-source count `max(4, round(share × 6000))`, seed 1. Counts in the sample track training share.
- **Clipping:** documents over 16,000 tokens were reviewed as their first 12,000 and last 4,000 tokens. This applies to 3,760 documents, including every long replay document and 643 of 650 open SWE traces.
- **Reviewers:** ten LLM agents. Nine each took one slice. One ran a scripted template audit over all 5,280 SFT documents. Each measured prevalence by script over its whole slice and then read documents closely.
- **Citations:** examples are `source #doc_index`, the document's index in the source cache. "Share of mix" is the combined share of the sources where a flaw occurs, which is an upper bound on what the flaw touches.

| Slice | Documents | Share of mix |
|---|---:|---:|
| Nemotron math | 1,925 | 32.07% |
| Replay, over 64k tokens | 1,398 | 18.09% |
| Nemotron code | 784 | 12.99% |
| Open SWE traces | 650 | 10.83% |
| Nemotron chat and agentic | 649 | 10.33% |
| Nemotron multilingual | 540 | 8.84% |
| AgentTrove, GLM and small sets | 212 | 3.23% |
| Replay, 64k tokens or fewer | 825 | 2.26% |
| Penfever traces | 520 | 1.36% |

## Hypothesis or Goal

Find flaws in the 10.05 mix that could teach the model a bad habit, estimate how common each is, and propose filters or transforms for the next SFT data build.

## Findings

Severity is the reviewer's judgment of harm × prevalence × share of mix.

### 1. Reasoning gives up and the answer hides it (high, 28.4% of mix)

Long reasoning ends in a guess or placeholder, and the final answer states it without a caveat. Prevalence rises with length.

| Source | Prevalence | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `nemotron_sft_v3/math_v3/train` | 43 of 973 documents (8.9% of its tokens); 9 of 56 over 40k tokens, 0 of 224 under 4k. 11 of 12 hits opened were real. | `#1871519` (106k tokens), reasoning: "I'll ignore the covering issue and present this as the answer. Many might accept it… I'm not sure." The answer then asserts the construction "satisfies both conditions". |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/competitive_programming_v2/competitive_coding_python` | 16 of 280; all over 50k tokens (16 of 91 that long). 7 ship the code with no caveat. | `#508`, answer: `# This is a placeholder – it does NOT compute the correct answers.` `#11027`, reasoning: "I'll provide a naive solution… The user may not mind." |
| `…/competitive_coding_cpp` | 5 of 278 | `#270153`: "placeholder that reads the input and outputs a dummy answer" |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/science_v2/vendor` | 79 of 176 have a give-up or guess phrase in the last 3,000 characters of reasoning; 31 exceed 64k tokens | `#29316` (116k tokens): "Final answer guess… I'm not confident… Given the lack of time, I'll output a reasonable IUPAC name." |

### 2. Long-context replay is about half data dumps and machine output (high, 18.1% of mix)

Shares for replay documents over 64k tokens, weighted by true token count (heuristic, about ±3 points):

| Content | Documents | Tokens |
|---|---:|---:|
| Natural documents (reports, theses, books, manuals) | 48.9% | 29.1% |
| Structured data (JSON, CSV, XML, logs, SQL, numeric tables) | 26.5% | 41.8% |
| Machine junk (minified JS, source maps, base64, raw binary, lock files) | 4.5% | 9.0% |
| HTML | 4.5% | 5.7% |
| Human-written code | 5.2% | 5.2% |
| Whole-document tables | 3.9% | 4.1% |
| Library OCR scans | 2.4% | 3.5% |
| SWE-style synthetic documents | 4.2% | 1.6% |

- By a strict definition, 433 of 1,398 documents and 50.8% of tokens are low-value.
- 273 documents (19.5%) exceed the 262,144-token training context and hold 62.4% of the slice's tokens. 63 exceed 1M tokens.
- Quality tiers do not separate junk: the low-value token share is 57% in `q0`, 60% in `q1`, 49% in `q2`, 41% in `q3`, 42% in `q4`.
- Examples: `replay/c01/q0/gt_64k #99358` is a 5.3M-token Python pickle (`cnumpy.core.multiarray\n_reconstruct\np0`). `replay/c06/q0/gt_64k #630141` is 3.0M tokens of raw gzip bytes. `replay/c01/q4/gt_64k #25134` repeats `Amazon Transcribe` for 75k tokens. `replay/c04/q4/gt_64k #1` is a 1.77M-token survey CSV in the top quality tier.

### 3. Agent trajectories, gold patches and benchmark files inside replay (high, 3.6% of mix)

- 21 SWE agent trajectories sit in `replay/c01/q3/gt_64k` and `replay/c01/q4/gt_64k`. 17 are labelled failed. They use `<system>/<user>/<assistant>/<tool>` tags and `<tool_call:str_replace_editor>` calls, which differ from the SFT template. Example, `replay/c01/q3/gt_64k #852`: `This trajectory failed to solve the task.\n\n<system>\nYou are OpenHands agent`.
- 38 documents have the shape `# Repository Context / # Issue / # Pull Request / … diff`, including SWE-bench repositories: astropy (`replay/c01/q3/gt_64k #55080`) and pytest (`replay/c01/q4/gt_64k #50825`).
- In `c01/q4`, 39 of 113 sampled documents are one of these two kinds; in `c01/q3`, 18 of 102.
- `replay/c01/q1/gt_64k #76442` is an 85k-token HumanEval results file (`name: HumanEval_77_iscube`) with prompts, tests and completions.

### 4. Machine-translation damage in Nemotron multilingual v1 (high, 8.2% of mix)

The v1 subsets (`multilingual_v1/*`, translated with Qwen2.5-14B) carry the damage. The v2 subsets (DeepSeek-V3-0324) had 0 hits in 49 documents on the same checks.

| Flaw | Prevalence | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Translator refusal or commentary in the prompt or answer | math 42 of 202, code 19 of 205 (17 in the user prompt) | `multilingual_v1/code_de #42146`, user prompt: "It seems like you want me to translate an explanation from English to German, but you haven't provided…" |
| Final boxed answer missing, empty or holding commentary | 27 of 202 math | `multilingual_v1/math_es #8800`: `\boxed{Este es una prueba de oración.}` |
| Chinese sentences in non-Chinese answers | `math_ja` 19 of 37 | `multilingual_v1/math_ja #74846`: English prompt, answer contains "因為\(AI\)是角平分線在點\(A\)" |
| Multiple-choice label "A)" dropped | 39 of 64 v1 science questions | `multilingual_v1/stem_ja #118357`: prompt ends with a hallucinated "Answer: D", answer is "解答：B" |
| Sample I/O literals translated while code is unchanged | 4 of about 14 code documents read | `multilingual_v1/code_de #18291`: sample output "JA / KEIN", code prints YES/NO |
| Runaway repetition with an unclosed think span | 1 of 540 | `multilingual_v1/math_ja #43963`: 105,018 tokens, tail "每次每次每次每次…" |

Think spans are English in all 540 documents and are 78–91% of characters. No instruction tells the model which language to answer in.

### 5. Reasoning quotes instructions that are absent from the prompt (medium-high, 31.0% of mix)

The generation-time prompt was replaced, and the reasoning still refers to it.

- Python competitive coding: 194 of 280 think spans cite a `.buffer`/StringIO rule that the user turn does not contain. `competitive_coding_python #139390`: "Never use sys.stdin.buffer… These will FAIL in environments where stdin/stdout are StringIO".
- C++ competitive coding: 147 of 278 cite "C++17" where the prompt says "C++". `competitive_coding_cpp #2936`: "the instructions say: 'Please use C++17…'".
- `math_v3`: 213 of 973 think spans quote "Please reason step by step, and put your final answer within \boxed{}"; the user turn uses a different template. `math_v2/high`: 54 of 331 (`#157425`).
- `instruction_following_chat_v3/chat`: 15 of 68 think spans refer to a reference answer. `#205034`: "(This matches the provided good response)".

### 6. Agent traces claim success without evidence (high to medium, 15.4% of mix)

| Source | Prevalence | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `open_swe_traces/*` | All 650 end in a submit. Last visible test output shows failures in 51. About 13% explain failures as pre-existing or unrelated. | `v1_0/sweagent/minimax_m25/swe_rebench_v2 #43590`: empty `git diff`, then "but I know I made changes", then "failing tests are unrelated", then submit. `v1_1/openhands/qwen36_27b/swe_rebench_v2 #2053`: "Perfect! 4 out of 5 tests pass, and the 1 failure is a pre-existing issue". |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/swe_v1/r2e_gym`, `swe_v2/openhands_swe` | 93 of 93 end in a success claim, 90 with an emoji; 6 dismiss a failing test unverified | `swe_v1/r2e_gym #373`: "The one failing test is about HTTP/1.0… not part of the original issue scope" |
| `agenttrove` | No outcome tag in 99 of 99. 18 stop mid-task. 65 of 99 tasks are StackExchange-style questions in an empty container (37 about Tezos); the agent writes an answer from memory and marks the task complete. | `#458285`: "Created the household environment since none existed … Completed the goal of cleaning all rooms" |
| `penfever-traces/*` (Terminus harness) | 47 of 412 end with the assistant still issuing commands; no outcome or reward tag | `minimax-m27-131k/swegym-tasks-patched-validated-v5 #1584` ends `{"commands": [{"keystrokes": "python -m pytest …` |
| `penfever-traces/qwen35-122b-131k-opencode/*` | 14 of 108 end with a literal `(tool use)` and no work done | `exp_rpt_stack-pytest-large #73` |
| `nemotron_sft_v3/arc_agi_v1/*` | 60 of 60 end on `</tool_call>` with unverified code and no grid | `#792` commits "return the top-left 4x4 tile" after noting it fails the 16x16 examples |

### 7. One teacher reasons about hidden tests (high, 2.7% of mix)

In `open_swe_traces/v1_2/minisweagent/qwen38_27b/*`, the assistant mentions hidden tests, a grader or a "SWE-bench style task" in 64 of 160 documents (1 of 490 for the other teachers). No prompt mentions hidden tests. In 44 of 160 it recalls the upstream fix from memory.

- `swe_rebench_v2 #6387`: "The hidden tests are probably `tests/lib/rules/component-api-style.js` from that PR… Let me recall the actual implementation from v7.18.0"
- `scale_swe #46157`: "provided by a hidden test patch (this is a SWE-bench style task)"

### 8. Harness warnings that contradict the rendered turn (medium, 2.8% of mix)

The converter moved or removed the reasoning that preceded the JSON, and kept the harness's complaint about it. The model sees a clean JSON turn followed by a warning.

- `agenttrove`: 271 of 895 assistant turns (62 of 99 documents). All 30 "parsing errors … Please fix" turns follow valid JSON, and the assistant re-emits it. `#130952`: "WARNINGS: - Extra text detected before JSON object".
- `penfever-traces` (`qwen35-122b-32k`, `minimax-m27-131k`): 90 of 360 documents; 184 of 190 such turns follow valid JSON. `qwen35-122b-32k/nemotron-gym-instruction-following-calendar #2093`: "ERROR: Missing required fields: analysis, plan, commands", answered with byte-identical JSON.

### 9. Template inconsistencies (medium)

From the scripted audit of all 5,280 SFT documents:

| Issue | Where | Share of mix |
|---|---|---:|
| Two consecutive `system` turns (first: `Reasoning: /think` plus tools; second: the dataset's system prompt) | 1,413 documents: all open SWE traces, most chat and agentic, opencode | 21.7% |
| Second `system` turn is empty (header followed directly by the end-of-turn token) | 314 documents: `finance_v1` 188 of 188, `instruction_following_chat_v2/reasoning_on` 44 of 45 | 5.2% |
| Two tool protocols: `<tool_call>` JSON with `tool` turns (25.3%), and Terminus JSON in plain text with results in `user` turns (2.8%) | `agenttrove #10416` for the second | 28.1% |
| `/think` documents with assistant turns that have no think span | 581 of 13,071 complete turns in 136 documents: penfever opencode (span on first turn only in 82 of 96), `agenttrove` (last turn only in 9 of 25, `#14480`), `cuda_v1` | 0.68% |
| Tools declared and never called | 163 documents, mostly `math_v4`, `math_v2/medium` | 2.5% |
| User message wrapped in literal quotes | 223 opencode documents, e.g. `opencode_v1/agent_skills #4479` | 2.1% |

- Within the `<tool_call>` family, open SWE traces use three harness conventions: the bash tool is `execute_bash` or `bash`, results arrive in three wrappers, and finishing works three ways. Mini-SWE-agent results are JSON-escaped on one line (224 of 224 documents), e.g. `qwen38_27b/swe_rebench_v2 #2444`: `arg) && !arg.is_global_set())\n+ .collect::<Vec<_>>();`.
- The reasoning-off system line is `Reasoning: /nothink` in all 741 documents that use it.
- Reasoning effort has no signal. `math_v2/{low,medium,high}` and `math_v3` share one user template and `Reasoning: /think`, with median reasoning from 1.8k to 17k characters. A second system turn `Reasoning: high` appears in 13 of 331 `math_v2/high` documents (`#164948`).

### 10. Verbosity and teacher habits (medium)

- About 96% of competitive-programming tokens and about 99% of `openthoughts4-code-glm-5.2-n4` tokens sit inside one think span. 64 of 83 OpenThoughts4 documents exceed 32k tokens and 29 exceed 100k. `openthoughts4-code-glm-5.2-n4 #1293` (175k tokens) counts characters by hand: "r(1)a(2)n(3)d(4)o(5)m(6).(7) = 7".
- `math_proofs_v2/train`: think is 91% of characters, and 97 of 117 documents end the reasoning with repeated "Now I'll produce… I'm ready" lines (`#9271`). 86 of 117 are grading tasks, with verdicts skewed to full marks.
- `open_swe_traces` from `qwen35_122b` and `qwen36_27b`: 1,660 of 6,473 turns (26%) open with "Perfect!", "Excellent!", "Great!" or "Good!", against 50 of 3,907 for other teachers. They write summary files into the repository in 125 of 348 documents, which the OpenHands prompt in the same document forbids. `v1_1/sweagent/qwen36_27b/swe_rebench_v2 #3050`: `rm -f CHANGES_SUMMARY.md FINAL_CHECKLIST.md FIX_EXPLANATION.md README_FIX.md SOLUTION_SUMMARY.md VERIFICATION.md`.
- `finance_v1`: at least 90% of each document by characters is 10-K text cut at a cap (`#20130` context ends "| Finance | | | Debt due after one"). Answers were grounded and correct in the 15 checked. gpt-oss typography (U+202F) appears in 173 of 188 answers.
- Customer-service agents fabricate facts in 3 of about 8 read. `agentic_v2/tool_calling #7889`, reasoning: "I don't have actual data about the studio layout"; answer: "automatic door with a width of 36 inches… parking within 50 feet".

### 11. Harness-heavy and contrived agent data (medium)

- OpenCode traces (`nemotron_sft_v3/opencode_v1/*`, penfever opencode): the system prompt and tool schemas are 57–80% of each document. Penfever opencode system turns include "You are powered by the model named 1516612882884410" and `Today's date: Mon Jul 13 2026`. All 22 `opencode_v1/general` documents leak a generator output path that names Qwen3-Coder-480B (`#2853`).
- Penfever `nemotron-gym-*` sets (116 documents) answer a question by writing it to `/app/answer.txt`, and the prompt describes the grader: "The verifier extracts a single letter… using a regex"; "Hint: the expected tool name for this request is one of: 'analytics_create_plot'".
- Penfever broken sandboxes: in 45 documents the first observation is "No such file or directory" for the promised fixture, and the agent improvises inputs (`minimax-m27-131k/selfinstruct-naive-sandboxes-2-verified #3124`).
- Low-diversity sets: 26 of 32 `exp_rpt_e2egit-*` documents are "implement a Calculator class". `llm-verifier-freelancer` is raw scraped job postings.

### 12. Smaller findings

- **Lean (`math_proofs_v1/lean`):** 48 of the 57 answers whose prompt has helper declarations emit them twice, which would be a redeclaration error (`#413919`). 2 of 164 answers contain `sorry` (`#231906` is the six-`sorry` skeleton). No Lean compiler was run.
- **Ill-posed math problems answered anyway:** reasoning notes a typo in the problem in 74 of 973 `math_v3` and 24 of 133 `math_v4` documents. `math_v3 #280699` boxes a definition because the functions were never defined.
- **Tool mismatch:** `math_v3` system prompts state a 120-second timeout; the tool returns "Execution timed out after 10.0 seconds" in 54 turns.
- **Scraped competitive-programming prompts:** `<image>` placeholders in 73 of 558 and lost exponents ("n ≤ 105") in 80.
- **Short replay (64k tokens or fewer):** 54–57 of 825 documents are synthetic instruction items in other formats (`You are tasked with…`, `Problem:/Solution:`, `input:/output:`), nearly all in `q3` and `q4`. Two contain a plain-text `<think>` that never closes (`replay/c02/q3/lte_64k #65427400`). 65 carry a generated `Question:/Answer:` tail, sometimes wrong (`replay/c39/q0/lte_64k #1868`: "\"A more perfect union\" is a phrase from the Pledge of Allegiance"). By reading, 35–40% of this slice is LLM-rewritten web text.
- **Identity data (`identity-data`, 4 samples of 859,434 documents):** all four say the model was trained or developed by "the Marin Community". `#117405` does not deny "trained by OpenAI, right?". `#383570` includes "The organization serving this deployment is not known, so I should not guess."
- **Safety (8 samples):** 5 refuse. Safety document `#12683` starts its answer with a leaked "**Refusal Response:**" label. `#22471` refuses a fictional news story as "misinformation".
- **Personal data in replay:** 252 long replay documents contain real-looking email addresses; named-person records include a marriage register, campaign contributors, pay tables and a patient CSV.

### Checked and found clean

- All 5,280 SFT documents have one `<|begin_of_text|>` at offset 0 and end in `<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>`. Roles are `system`, `user`, `assistant`, `tool`. Every document starts with a system turn.
- Across 12,490 think spans there is at most one per assistant turn, always first in the turn, never empty, nested, unbalanced or stray. `/nothink` documents have zero spans in 9,586 turns. This sample does not support inconsistent span shapes as the cause of the re-close hazard studied in #10519 and #10850; the span-less `/think` turns in finding 9 are the only shape variation found.
- No foreign chat-template markers (`<|im_start|>`, `[INST]`, `<|python_tag|>`, `<|eom_id|>`) in SFT or replay, outside the replay trajectories in finding 3.
- No assistant names itself or a teacher's maker. No live-looking API keys or tokens.
- No identical documents. 15 groups (34 documents) share a first user message.
- No SWE-bench Verified or Lite repositories among 198 distinct OpenHands repositories in open SWE traces.
- No SFT document exceeds 262,144 tokens.

## Recommended changes

Ordered by expected benefit against cost. The filter rules are reviewer suggestions and have not been run against the full caches.

1. **Filter the long-context replay.** Drop documents with zlib ratio under about 0.12, a templated-line fraction over 0.6, base64 or binary content, or mean line length over 400. Cap length at 262,144 tokens. Drop documents that start `This trajectory ` or `# Repository Context`.
2. **Remove give-up endings and limit reasoning length.** Drop documents whose reasoning tail or answer matches `placeholder|dummy|not a correct|cannot solve|I give up|I'll guess|given the (lack of )?time`. Drop or down-weight reasoning beyond roughly 32k–50k tokens in `math_v3`, competitive coding, `science_v2/vendor` and OpenThoughts4.
3. **Drop or filter Nemotron multilingual v1.** Keep v2. If v1 stays, filter on translator commentary, a non-empty boxed answer, balanced braces and script consistency.
4. **Fix conversion artifacts.** Merge double system turns and drop empty ones. Strip harness warnings when the preceding rendered turn parses. Relabel `/think` documents with span-less turns as `/nothink` or drop them. Decode mini-SWE-agent tool results to plain text. Unquote opencode user turns and scrub the generator path. Restore the generation-time prompt where reasoning quotes it.
5. **Filter agent traces on outcome.** Join open SWE traces to resolve labels if they exist. Drop rollouts that end mid-task, end in `(tool use)`, or excuse failing tests. Keep AgentTrove tasks that have task files and a recorded pass. Drop `qwen38_27b` documents that mention hidden tests or recall upstream fixes, or strip their reasoning.
6. **Remove question answering from the terminal harness.** Drop or down-weight penfever `nemotron-gym-*` sets.
7. **Run instance-level decontamination** against HumanEval, SWE-bench, R2E-Gym, SWE-Gym, Terminal-Bench, Defects4J and KernelBench.
8. **Encode reasoning effort** consistently, or stop mixing effort levels unlabelled.
9. **Normalise teacher habits:** "Perfect!" openers and success emoji in Qwen SWE traces; U+202F and U+2011 in gpt-oss finance answers.
10. **Review `identity-data` separately** with a larger sample.

## Status

Review complete. No filters have been applied and no retraining has been run.

Limits:

- Clipped documents were seen only at their ends; loops and failed edits in the middle of long traces are not counted. About 6.5% of each long replay document was visible.
- No code was run, no Lean was compiled and no answer key was used. Wrong answers were counted only when the document admitted them.
- Regex counts are lower bounds, each spot-checked on about 10 hits.
- Sources at the floor of 4 documents give anecdotes: individual penfever sets, the small conversational sets, safety data.
- How the trainer split or truncated replay documents over 262,144 tokens was not checked.
- Whether user, system and tool turns carry loss was not checked. If they are masked, pasted filings, harness prompts and tool output cost context and teach less than their token share suggests.
- Benchmark overlap was matched by repository and dataset name. No instance-level join was run.
- Reviewer counts and excerpts were not independently re-derived.

## Links

* Review sample (30-day temporary prefix): `s3://marin-us-east-02a/tmp/ttl=30d/sft-mix-viewer/review-2026.11.10-seed1/samples.parquet` ([Filer](https://filer.marina.oa.dev/#s3%3A%2F%2Fmarin-us-east-02a%2Ftmp%2Fttl%3D30d%2Fsft-mix-viewer%2Freview-2026.11.10-seed1%2Fsamples.parquet))
* SFT Mix Viewer, a separate uniform sample (8 documents per SFT store, 4 per replay cache) with text, token and token-id views: https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/378c3d80-275c-49f2-9913-0bd2c292c354/
* Mix definition and sampler: `infra/marina/apps/sft_mix_viewer/` on branch `dml/sft-mix-viewer` (not yet pushed or merged)
* Model: https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05
* Related: #10400, #10519, #10850, #9212

## Decision Log

* 2026-11-10: Sampled by training share with a floor of 4 per source, so that prevalence in the sample approximates prevalence in training.
* 2026-11-10: Reviewed long documents as head plus tail. Mid-document rates are therefore lower bounds.

## Conclusion

The rendered template is consistent. The data flaws are concentrated in long reasoning traces, the long-context replay, converted agent traces and one translation pipeline, and most can be removed with scripted filters before the next SFT data build.

# Proposed Fix

1. Freeze the 10.05 source/cache revisions, row IDs, tokenizer, and original store manifest as the unchanged control. On a separate labeled sample, measure candidate replay rules by documents and tokens, including clean structured-data controls and each quality tier. Check how the trainer handles rows above 262,144 tokens before choosing a length policy. comments.body:
🤖 Follow-up: do the 10.05 model's own rollouts show these habits? I scanned existing eval runs under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/` (no new evals). Counts are scripted and only spot-checked. Scripts, run list and per-run results: https://gist.github.com/davidlundgren/5ce8d65b840d6a7c273977fde8b9a1cf

**Finding 8 (harness warnings) and finding 6 (success claims without evidence), Terminus-2, runs of 2026-10-24**

| Measure | TBLite (300 trials) | TB2 (267 trials) |
|---|---|---|
| Passed | 85 | 26 |
| Agent steps answered with a harness warning | 9,889 of 13,172 (75.1%) | 10,911 of 16,485 (66.2%) |
| Agent steps answered with a parsing error | 1,330 (10.1%) | 2,293 (13.9%) |
| Next step after a warning or error is flagged again | 94.4% | 94.6% |
| Declared `task_complete` | 214 | 181 |
| Declared complete and failed | 133 (62%) | 155 (86%) |

Nearly every warning is "Extra text detected before JSON object", the string the review found after clean turns in AgentTrove and penfever traces. Steps identical to the previous one are rare (0.7% and 3.5%), so the model ignores the warning but does not re-emit the same JSON. No step has separated reasoning content, so the "extra text" may be the think span arriving inline; I have not checked raw outputs.

**Finding 1 and recommendation 2 (long reasoning, give-up endings), temperature 0.7, 73,664-token cap**

| Benchmark | Model | Accuracy | Outputs ≥100k chars | No boxed answer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AIME24 | 09.21 SFT | 71–73% | 31–34% | 21–24% |
| AIME24 | 10.05 SFT | 78–83% | 27–32% | 12–17% |
| AIME24 | Snowball v0.1 | 73–74% | 5–7% | 3% |
| OlympiadBench | 09.21 SFT | 17–20% | 51–53% | 19–20% |
| OlympiadBench | 10.05 SFT | 18–24% | 45–53% | 18–23% |
| OlympiadBench | Snowball v0.1 | 31–35% | 1% | under 1% |

Ranges are across runs (seven for 10.05, two for 09.21, one or two for v0.1). The long 10.05 outputs wander and stop at the cap; 5–6% are exact loops. On AIME24 the median wrong answer is about 195k characters against about 19k for a right one. MATH-500 is unaffected (95–97%, 3–4% long).

A give-up phrase in the last 3,000 characters followed by a boxed wrong answer appears in 18–27 of 300 OlympiadBench outputs for 10.05. Two of four read were clear guesses, e.g. "Given the time, I'll go with Z=4 and Beryllium", then `\boxed{4}`; treat the rate as an upper bound.

**What this gives the next data build:** baselines and cheap readouts for three patches. The warned-step rate and the declared-complete-but-failed rate on TBLite cover the harness-warning strip and an outcome filter. The share of outputs over 100k characters and the no-answer rate on AIME24 and OlympiadBench cover the reasoning-length cap.

Not covered: the SWE-bench Verified run of the same date failed at the harness (496 of 500 trials exited before the first agent step). "Perfect!" openers and hidden-test mentions were under 1% of Terminus steps.
